subject.title: Cross-provider fallback should respect provider trust boundaries for images/attachments

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit provider media trust policy for cross-provider fallback, or treat configured fallback providers as trusted for all current-turn media?
rationale: The source path is clear, but the correct default changes the security boundary and upgrade expectations for existing fallback users.

options.title: Add explicit media trust policy
options.body: Add a documented config surface and runtime checks so users can opt out of cross-provider image/attachment transfer while preserving existing behavior by default unless maintainers choose otherwise.

options.title: Document fallback as media consent
options.body: Keep runtime behavior and document that adding a provider to fallback means that provider may receive the current turn's media payloads.

options.title: Strip media on cross-provider fallback
options.body: Fail closed by default for cross-provider media, accepting a compatibility break only with maintainer security approval and upgrade proof.

recommendation.title: Add explicit media trust policy
recommendation.body: Add a documented config surface and runtime checks so users can opt out of cross-provider image/attachment transfer while preserving existing behavior by default unless maintainers choose otherwise.

likelyOwner.reason: They recently changed the affected CLI fallback image path and are best positioned among the observed history owners to judge the runtime compatibility tradeoff.
